meta.title: GentStore — GUI for Portage on Gentoo Linux
meta.description: It shows what it will do before it does it. Package search, USE flags with explanations, masks, licences and overlays — in one window, never as root.

hero.lead: A graphical front-end for Portage on Gentoo Linux. Searching for and installing packages, USE flags with an explanation of what each one does, masks and licences, overlays, and the full system update cycle.
hero.note: Every change to `/etc/portage` is previewed before it is written. The interface never runs as root.

principles.title: Five rules the whole application stands on
principles.lead: Not slogans — each one has a specific consequence in the interface, visible on screen before anything is written.

rules.title: Nothing happens quietly
rules.body: Every change to `/etc/portage` is previewed before it is written, and afterwards the application shows the exact path of the file and the exact line it added. Every button that executes a command has a tooltip with the command in full.

rules.title: We never overwrite your files
rules.body: We append lines, or change one specific line; comments and the formatting of the rest of the file are left untouched.

rules.title: The graphical process is not root
rules.body: Everything that needs privileges goes through `pkexec` and a small, reviewable helper program.

rules.title: The data comes from the `portage` API
rules.body: Not from parsing ebuilds. The `core/` layer is plain Python with no Qt — it can be queried from a terminal.

rules.title: The chosen repository applies everywhere
rules.body: Clicking a `::repo` badge narrows not only the list but also the detail panel, the versions, and the atom `emerge` is given. The same package in two overlays no longer blurs together.

screens.title: The whole Portage cycle, screen by screen
screens.shortcuts: `Ctrl+1…9` switches screens, `Ctrl+F` jumps to the search box, `Ctrl+L` to the log.

entries.title: Search and install
entries.body: Searching by name, category and description. Repository filters, a list of versions, and the Pretend, Install and Uninstall actions — each shows the exact command before it runs it.

entries.title: System update
entries.body: Six steps, each run separately: sync, Gentoo news, a preview in the form of a table, the update itself with a live log and an “Interrupt” button, `--depclean`, and the configuration files.

entries.title: Repositories
entries.body: What you have configured, with the `repos.conf` section verbatim — and the catalogue of Gentoo repositories in the second tab. Enabling an overlay is one click.

entries.title: Masks and licences
entries.body: Why Portage refuses: for a mask, the maintainer's note verbatim along with the file it came from; for keywords, three cases told apart; for a licence, the full text to read.

entries.title: Configuration files
entries.body: The `._cfg` files, with the package that brought each one and the number of changed lines. Next to it the difference, and under that three answers: keep mine, take the new one, merge by hand.

entries.title: make.conf
entries.body: Two values for each variable: the one written in the file and the one Portage actually uses. A change replaces one line. `MAKEOPTS` gets a suggestion computed from the core count and the amount of memory. `EMERGE_DEFAULT_OPTS` is editable here and applies to the `emerge` you run in a terminal — not to the ones this window runs, which ignore it so that the command shown before a run is the whole of what runs.

entries.title: elog messages
entries.body: What packages said about themselves during installation — the messages that scroll past in the terminal and vanish. Each entry has a class and a build phase, and the left edge of the row carries the colour of the most serious message inside it.

entries.title: @world set
entries.body: Side by side, two things that look identical once installed: the packages you asked for, and everything that is installed. Removing an entry uninstalls nothing.

entries.title: Profile
entries.body: The profiles from `eselect`, with the current one marked and, before a change, what follows from it said plainly: different default USE flags, different masks, a full rebuild.

use_flags.title: A USE flag stops being a guess
paragraphs: For each flag you can see where its value comes from — the ebuild, the profile, `make.conf`, `package.use` — and the description from the repository.

Unfolded: exactly what turning it on changes, which packages will be pulled in and which ones will have the same flag forced on them. `REQUIRED_USE` conditions are checked as you go, and saving is blocked until the selection satisfies them.
At the bottom of the panel, the exact line that will go into the file, and the file it will be appended to — before anything happens.

privileges.title: GentStore never runs as root
paragraphs: Started with `sudo` it says so in a dialog and asks to be closed. Everything that needs privileges goes through `pkexec` and two small programs in `/usr/libexec`.

Both are single files that use nothing but the standard library, with no imports from the rest of the project — written so that they can be read end to end before being let anywhere near root. It is worth doing.

Every privileged step asks for your password. Both polkit actions are `auth_admin`, not the form that remembers an answer for a few minutes, so a six-step system update asks six times. What that form remembers is not **this window may carry on** but **this user has authenticated for this action** — and anything else running as you could use it.
Without the privileged half the application still runs — read-only: search, browsing flags, `emerge --pretend`. Every attempt to write then says what is missing.

files.note: the only program that writes to /etc/portage
runs emerge and friends, and can interrupt them

install.title: Two routes
install.lead: The choice comes down to whether Portage should know about GentStore.

routes.title: Through Portage — a local overlay
routes.note: No clone needed. Fetch the script, read it, run it.
routes.body: The script registers `/var/db/repos/gentstore` as a synced overlay — later ebuilds arrive with an ordinary `emerge --sync`. It prints every file it writes and overwrites nobody else's. **Reading it first is the version this project recommends** — 200 lines, and it is about to run as root.

routes.title: From the working directory — for working on the code
routes.note: The `.qm` catalogues are not kept in the repository.
routes.body: You get the tagged release, unless you say otherwise — the installer asks, and `--stable` and `--live` skip the question. The `9999` ebuild sorts above every release there will ever be, so choosing the release means the live one is deliberately left unaccepted.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.footnote: Optional: `app-portage/gentoolkit` (GLSA scanning) and `app-portage/cpuid2cpuflags`. Their absence disables a single feature and is reported in the interface — it does not bring the application down.

cli.title: The backend without the GUI
cli.lead: The `core/` layer is plain Python with no Qt, so it can be queried from a terminal. Useful when a list in the window is empty and you need to know whether the problem is in the interface or in the data.
cli.footnote: Every command takes `--json` and `--debug`. It is a development tool — it speaks English only, because it is not part of the interface.

status.title: Version 1.3.5
status.body: All nine screens work, and both halves have been exercised on a live system: the read-only side — search, USE flags, masks, repositories, the update preview, configuration files, `make.conf`, elog and `@world` — and the privileged one, which has written real `package.use`, `package.license` and `package.accept_keywords` entries through `pkexec`.

caveat.title: What that number does not claim
caveat.body: 797 tests pass, but this has run on **one** machine, amd64 only — so the ebuild is keyworded `~amd64`. The package announces itself as `Development Status :: 4 - Beta`, which is the same statement said twice on purpose. Bug reports from other setups are the fastest way to make the next release better.

changes.title: The Repositories screen is one list with two tabs
changes.body: “Configured” and “Available” are the same question asked at different times. One search box serves whichever tab is open, and picking a row fills the right side — for a configured repository, also **what it brings**: the packages that come from it and nowhere else.

changes.title: Three holes in the privileged half closed
changes.body: `emerge --unmerge '*/*'` passed the launcher's argument check; the helper answered a malformed request with a traceback instead of an answer; `cfg_apply` could be aimed outside `/etc/portage`. A failed restore no longer takes the configuration root with it.

changes.title: USE flags of a package from an overlay finally have descriptions
changes.body: `use.desc` lives in the master repository, and it was being looked for beside the ebuild, where no overlay carries it.

changes.title: 1.1.1 is withdrawn
changes.body: The release, its asset and its tag are deleted, and the ebuild is out of the overlay, so Portage cannot resolve to a version that cannot be built. The changelog keeps the section, marked `[YANKED]` — a withdrawn release is a fact about the project.

settings.title: Polish and English, switched on the fly
paragraphs: The language comes from the system settings; `View → Language` changes it without a restart. The interface scale — 100, 115 or 130% — is under `View → Interface size`, because the 12.5 px base font is small on purpose: the screens show a lot of data at once.
The settings also carry how the application becomes root, and how many copies of `/etc/portage` to keep.

cta.title: Install it and see what Portage was trying to tell you
cta.body: The script stops short of installing anything and prints the command instead. You run it yourself.
